children: ("Monteoro" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the commencement of a high-resolution, drone-borne (UAV) magnetic, gamma-ray spectrometric (radiometric) and LiDAR survey over its Nudillales copper-gold-molybdenum-silver project ("Nudillales" or the "Project"), located in the municipality of Dabeiba, Antioquia, Colombia. The survey is the first step in the Company's pre-drilling target refinement program at Nudillales, and is designed to more precisely define the geology, alteration and structure beneath a large surface geochemical footprint, ahead of planned diamond drilling.
Data acquisition commenced on November 13, 2026 and is expected to take approximately 25 days to complete.
227 line-kilometres over 951 hectares, flown at 50-metre line spacing and a nominal terrain clearance of 50 metres, covering both the Nudillales intrusive suite and Tabaco and Charcohondo targets.
Three datasets in a single program:

Magnetics, radiometrics and LiDAR topography will be collected concurrently to support geological, hydrothermal alteration and structural interpretation in areas of extensive vegetation and soil cover.

Results will be integrated with existing surface geochemistry and geological and alteration mapping to prioritize targets for the approximately 5,000-metre drill program planned at Nudillales, for which drilling permits are in place.
"Nudillales is a largely untested copper-gold-molybdenum system, and this survey is a major step toward positioning our first drill holes,"
Bob Neill, Chief Executive Officer of Monteoro Minerals

Launching this program within weeks of our listing reflects our commitment to advancing our flagship projects quickly and systematically. High-resolution magnetics and radiometrics are among the most effective tools for vectoring toward the core of intrusion-related Cu-Au-Mo systems like Nudillales. Combined with the strong surface geochemistry already outlined at Nudillales, this dataset will allow our technical team to spot our first drill holes with considerably greater confidence."

The survey is being carried out by Geoscan Ingeniería using UAV (drone) platforms. Magnetic and gamma-ray spectrometric data are being acquired along east–west flight lines spaced 50 metres apart, with tie lines spaced 250 metres apart, at a nominal mean terrain clearance of 50 metres. LiDAR data acquired over the same area will produce a high-resolution digital terrain model of the Project.

Low-altitude, drone-borne surveys allow data to be collected close to the ground in steep, forested terrain, providing the potential for higher spatial resolution compared with conventional fixed-wing or helicopter-borne surveys. Key survey specifications are summarized in Table 1.
Magnetics (MAG), gamma-ray spectrometry (RAD) and LiDAR topography
Table 1: Nudillales UAV geophysical and LiDAR survey specifications

The survey was designed to better define geology, alteration and structure across the significant surface geochemical footprint at Nudillales and is expected to be fundamental to defining targets for follow-up drilling. Specific objectives are to:

Identify strong, well-defined magnetic contrasts associated with intrusive-related mineralization, as reflected by magnetite-rich intrusives and alteration zones, as well as overprinting magnetite-destructive alteration events;

Use potassium, thorium and uranium radiometric data to assist in identifying potassium rich intrusive phases, potential zones of potassic alteration and lithological contacts between plutons of contrasting composition;
Define the structural framework, including faults, shear zones and intrusive contacts, that may control the distribution of magmato-hydrothermal feeder zones and mineralization;
Generate a high-resolution LiDAR -based terrain model to support geological and structural interpretation, as well as planning of drill pads and access; and
Pinpoint high-priority zones potentially associated with magmatic-hydrothermal mineralization for follow-up diamond drilling.

Situated approximately 160 km NW of Medellin, Nudillales is road-accessible, being traversed by the Panamerican Highway en route to open-ocean port facilities located on the Gulf of Uraba, an additional 120 km further NW. Monteoro's mineral titles host an outcropping but largely untested, intrusion-related copper-gold-molybdenum-silver system, associated with the Nudillales suite, a km-scale, polyphase diorite-quartz diorite-quartz monzonite-aplite intrusive complex. Historical soil sampling outlined a copper-in-soil anomaly defining a target area of approximately 400 metres by 600 metres, containing more localized gold, molybdenum and silver values. Historical rock sampling has returned copper, gold and molybdenum values associated with zones of strong to intense fracturing, magmato-hydrothermal brecciation, replacement of mafic phases by magnetite, and potassic (K-feldspar-biotite) +/- quartz, sericite and pyrite alterations. Chalcopyrite +/- bornite and molybdenite occur as fracture fillings and disseminations in diorite-quartz diorite and aplite as well as in fragments within brecciated quartz monzonite. Two principal targets, Tabaco and Charcohondo, have been identified to date, and will be described in more detail in future press releases relating to the geology and geochemistry of the zone.
